newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends higher on cold, short-covering.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends higher on cold, short-covering.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures settled higher on a mix of short covering and lingering fears over damage to the U.S. HRW crop from bitter cold weather in the U.S. Midwest, traders said.

"I think a lot of this is technical short covering by the commissions, which is a little surprising," one trader said. "We should be seeing resistance somehwere between ($4.10 and $4.14 in the KCBT March contract), but so far this thing isn't showing signs of lying down."
Traders said the mostly light holiday-type volume helped accentuate the market's gains.
KCBT wheat closed one to six cents per bushel higher, with Dec up six cents at $4.54. March gained 2-1/2 cents to close at $4.11, its highest close since it settled at $4.11-1/2 on Oct 18.
Pressure came in the form of spillover weakness from CBOT wheat and Farmland's announced delivery of 150,000 bushels of wheat against the March KCBT contract.
Traders said FIMAT bought 1.6 million March bushels and sold 600,000 March. Refco bought one million March. CIS bought 1.4 million March and sold two milion March.
